q: Which poet is honoured as the 'Adi Kavi' (first poet) of Gujarati literature?
e: Narsinh Mehta, the 15th-century bhakti poet of Junagadh, is regarded as the Adi Kavi of Gujarati.

q: The bhajan 'Vaishnav Jan To Tene Kahiye', a favourite of Gandhiji, was composed by:
e: This bhajan describing a true devotee was written by Narsinh Mehta.

q: Garba is mainly performed during which festival?
e: Garba is danced in circles around a lamp or image of the Goddess during the nine nights of Navratri.

q: Uttarayan, Gujarat's famous kite-flying festival, falls on the day of:
e: Uttarayan coincides with Makar Sankranti (usually 14 January), when the sun begins its northward journey.

q: Which temple in Gujarat is regarded as the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas?
e: Somnath on the Saurashtra coast is traditionally counted first among the twelve Jyotirlingas.

q: The main temple of Dwarkadhish at Dwarka is also known as:
e: The principal shrine of Lord Krishna as Dwarkadhish at Dwarka is called Jagat Mandir.

q: Ambaji, one of the major Shakti Peeths, is located in which district?
e: Ambaji temple is in Danta taluka of Banaskantha district.

q: The Patola, a double-ikat silk saree, is traditionally woven at:
e: Patan's Salvi families are famous for the double-ikat Patola.

q: The Tarnetar fair is held near which temple?
e: The Tarnetar fair is held at the Trinetreshwar Mahadev temple in Surendranagar district in the month of Bhadrapad.

q: The Bhavnath fair at the foot of Girnar is held on the occasion of:
e: Sadhus and pilgrims gather at Bhavnath Mahadev, Junagadh, for the Mahashivratri fair.

q: The Vautha fair, well known for donkey and camel trading, is held in which district?
e: Vautha, in Dholka taluka of Ahmedabad district, hosts the fair on Kartik Purnima at a meeting point of several rivers.

q: The Sun Temple at Modhera was built during the reign of which ruler?
e: The Modhera Sun Temple in Mehsana district dates to 1026-27 CE, in the reign of Solanki king Bhimdev I.

q: The Adalaj stepwell near Gandhinagar is associated with which queen?
e: Adalaj Vav was completed in 1499 by Queen Rudabai, wife of the Vaghela chief Veer Singh.

q: The Jain temple complex of Palitana is located on which hill?
e: Palitana in Bhavnagar district has hundreds of Jain temples on the Shatrunjaya hill.

q: In which town of Kheda district is the famous Ranchhodraiji temple located?
e: The Ranchhodraiji (Krishna) temple at Dakor in Kheda district draws large crowds, especially on full-moon days.

q: Siddi Dhamal dance is performed by the Siddi community, whose ancestors came from:
e: The Siddis of Gujarat, settled mainly around Jambur near Gir, trace their roots to East Africa.

q: Tippani, a folk dance in which women beat the floor with long wooden poles, belongs to which area?
e: Tippani grew out of the work of women labourers of the Chorwad area who pounded floors with poles while singing.

q: Asait Thakar is regarded as the father of which traditional folk theatre form of Gujarat?
e: Asait Thakar (14th century) is credited with creating the Bhavai folk theatre and its many 'vesh' (plays).

q: Rogan art, painting with castor-oil-based paint on cloth, is mainly practised today at:
e: Rogan painting survives mainly with a few artisan families of Nirona in Kutch.

q: Who was the first Gujarati writer to receive the Jnanpith Award?
e: Umashankar Joshi received the Jnanpith Award in 1967 for his poetry collection 'Nishith'.

q: The famous four-part Gujarati novel 'Saraswatichandra' was written by:
e: Govardhanram Tripathi wrote 'Saraswatichandra' in four parts between 1887 and 1901.

q: The poem 'Jay Jay Garavi Gujarat' was written by:
e: Narmad (Narmadashankar Dave) wrote 'Jay Jay Garavi Gujarat', a celebrated song of Gujarati pride.

q: Which poet was given the title 'Rashtriya Shayar' by Mahatma Gandhi?
e: Gandhiji called Zaverchand Meghani 'Rashtriya Shayar' for his patriotic songs.

q: The poet Kalapi, author of 'Kalapi no Kekarav', was the ruler of which princely state?
e: Kalapi was Sursinhji Gohil, the prince of Lathi in Saurashtra.

q: Which Gujarati poet is famous for 'Akhyans' such as 'Sudama Charit' and 'Okhaharan'?
e: Premanand (17th century), the master of the Akhyan form, wrote 'Sudama Charit', 'Okhaharan' and 'Nalakhyan'.

q: Which work is regarded as the first original novel in Gujarati?
e: Nandshankar Mehta's 'Karan Ghelo' (1866) is considered the first Gujarati novel.

q: The Gujarati Sahitya Parishad was founded in 1905 at the initiative of:
e: Ranjitram Vavabhai Mehta took the initiative; the Ranjitram Suvarna Chandrak is named after him.

q: Which writer of 'Patan ni Prabhuta' also founded the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan?
e: Kanaiyalal Maneklal Munshi wrote historical novels on Patan and founded Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan in 1938.

q: The Rann Utsav, a festival of the white salt desert, is held in which district?
e: The Rann Utsav is held in winter near Dhordo on the white Rann of Kutch.

q: Pavagadh hill is famous for the temple of which goddess?
e: The Mahakali temple stands atop Pavagadh in Panchmahal district.
